claims.statement: UNESCO describes the monumental city’s building period broadly as the first through seventh centuries CE.
Large pyramids and temples formed part of a city laid out according to geometric and symbolic principles.
The map uses UNESCO’s reference position for Teotihuacán’s monumental city, not a territorial boundary.

evidence.note: The full source period extends beyond 200 CE. Monuments belong to different phases; this does not imply all were present in the first century or that settlement began in 1 CE. The map marker locates the archaeological site.
